songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Smokestack Lightning duel, rare St Stephen sandwich, soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The set opens with a monster Smokestack Lightning that showcases Jerry and Bob's fierce guitar duel. Highlights include a rare Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Saint Stephen sandwich, an expansive Turn On Your Lovelight, and strong Dark Star explorations. The performance stays tight throughout despite the matrix mix’s low drum levels.
ai_show_review.review: Feb 8‑1970 at the Fillmore West captures a Grateful Dead that was firing on all cylinders. Pigpen leads with a thunderous Smokestack Lightning that turns into an exhilarating guitar duel between Jerry and Bob, setting a high bar for the evening. The first set rolls smoothly through Morning Dew, a soulful It Hurts Me Too, and the classic China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue, each spotlit by Garcia’s lyrical phrasing and Weir’s responsive rhythm. The second set delivers one of the era’s most talked‑about moments—a Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Saint Stephen sandwich that builds tension then releases it into a soaring Turn On Your Lovelight, which stretches out for over half an hour and remains a benchmark jam from this period. Dark Star adds another deep exploratory stretch before the band wraps up with the blues‑y punch of Lovelight. While the matrix source is only fair—drums sit low in the mix and occasional dropouts bite—the musical chemistry shines through, making this show a must‑listen for fans of early‑’70 Dead intensity.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Multiple recordings praise standout moments—Smokestack Lightning duel, rare St Stephen > Not Fade Away > St Stephen sandwich, and a marathon Lovelight—indicating strong positive sentiment about the performance despite mixed comments on recording quality.

best_recording.reason: Fair matrix tape but the most complete and consistently praised for capturing the stellar performance, especially the Lovelight stretch.

key_highlights: Smokestack Lightning duel between Jerry and Bob sets a high‑energy tone.
Rare Saint Stephen > Not Fade Away > Saint Stephen sandwich adds tension and surprise.
Turn On Your Lovelight expands into a 35‑minute jam that defines the era’s improvisational peak.
Strong Dark Star and China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider interplay showcase tight group chemistry.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar shines, especially in the Smokestack Lightning duel and the soaring solos on China Cat Sunflower and Lovelight.
band_performance.Bob: Weir matches Jerry note‑for‑note on Smokestack Lightning and adds vocal intensity during the St Stephen return.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are solid and drive the jams, though they sit low in the matrix mix.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s percussion provides a steady backbone throughout; performance remains tight despite being buried in the recording.
